field.card: Reddit — Would anyone mind explaining to me like I'm 5 what the singularity is?
YouTube — The Singularity is Coming (Absolutely Agentic, 19:19)

F1.quote: "The technological singularity, often simply called the singularity, is a hypothetical event in which technological growth accelerates beyond human control, producing unpredictable changes in human civilization."
F1.claim: The singularity is a hypothetical event in which technological growth accelerates beyond human control

F2.quote: "According to the most popular version of the singularity hypothesis, I. J. Good's intelligence explosion model of 1965, an upgradable intelligent agent could eventually enter a positive feedback loop of successive self-improvement cycles"
F2.claim: The most popular version is Good's 1965 intelligence explosion model: self-improvement cycles in positive feedback

F3.quote: "Prominent technologists and academics dispute the plausibility of a technological singularity and associated artificial intelligence "explosion", including Paul Allen, Jeff Hawkins, John Holland, Jaron Lanier, Steven Pinker, Theodore Modis, Gordon Moore, and Roger Penrose."
F3.claim: Prominent technologists and academics dispute its plausibility

F4.quote: "One claim is that artificial intelligence growth is likely to run into decreasing returns instead of accelerating ones."
F4.claim: One objection: AI growth will meet decreasing returns

F5.quote: "Stuart J. Russell and Peter Norvig observe that in the history of technology, improvement in a particular area tends to follow an S curve: it begins with accelerating improvement, then levels off without continuing upward into a hyperbolic singularity."
F5.claim: Russell and Norvig: technological improvement follows an S curve

F6.quote: "But a technological singularity is not required for machines that can perform at or beyond a human level on certain tasks to be developed, nor does their existence imply the possibility of such an occurrence"
F6.claim: Human-level task performance neither requires nor implies a singularity

F7.quote: "The Hungarian-American mathematician John von Neumann is the first person known to have discussed a "singularity" in technological progress."
F7.claim: Von Neumann is the first known to discuss a technological 'singularity'

F8.quote: "Stanislaw Ulam reported in 1958 that an earlier discussion with von Neumann "centered on the accelerating progress of technology and changes in human life, which gives the appearance of approaching some essential singularity in the history of the race beyond which human affairs, as we know them, could not continue"."
F8.claim: Ulam (1958): a singularity beyond which human affairs could not continue

F9.quote: "Thus the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention that man need ever make, provided that the machine is docile enough to tell us how to keep it under control."
F9.claim: Good: the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention, provided it is docile enough

F10.quote: "The concept and the term "singularity" were popularized by Vernor Vinge, first in a 1983 op-ed in Omni magazine"
F10.claim: Vinge popularized the term, first in a 1983 Omni op-ed

F11.quote: "In his 1993 essay "The Coming Technological Singularity", Vinge wrote that the transition would signal the end of the human era"
F11.claim: Vinge 1993: the transition would end the human era

F12.quote: "he would be surprised if it occurred before 2005 or after 2030"
F12.claim: Vinge: surprised if before 2005 or after 2030

F13.quote: "Another significant contribution to wider circulation of the notion was Ray Kurzweil's 2005 book The Singularity Is Near, predicting singularity by 2045."
F13.claim: Kurzweil's 2005 book circulated the notion, predicting 2045

F14.quote: "I. J. Good, Vernor Vinge, and Ray Kurzweil define the concept in terms of the technological creation of super intelligence, arguing that it is difficult or impossible for present-day humans to predict what human beings' lives would be like in a post-singularity world"
F14.claim: Good, Vinge, Kurzweil: a post-singularity world is hard or impossible to predict

F15.quote: "The related concept of "speed superintelligence" describes an artificial intelligence that can function like a human mind but much faster."
F15.claim: Speed superintelligence: a human-like mind running much faster

F16.quote: "Technology forecasters and researchers disagree about when, or whether, human intelligence will be surpassed."
F16.claim: Forecasters disagree on when or whether human intelligence will be surpassed

F17.quote: "Some writers use "the singularity" in a broader way, to refer to any radical changes in society brought about by new technology (such as molecular nanotechnology), although Vinge and other writers say that without superintelligence, such changes would not be a true singularity."
F17.claim: A broader use covers any radical technological change; Vinge denies it is a true singularity without superintelligence

F18.quote: "It is unclear whether an intelligence explosion resulting in a singularity would be beneficial or harmful, or even an existential threat."
F18.claim: Unclear whether beneficial, harmful or existential threat

F19.quote: "There is not the slightest reason to believe in a coming singularity."
F19.claim: Pinker: no reason to believe in a coming singularity

F20.quote: "The singularity is the point where AI surpasses human intelligence and can improve itself better than humans can."
F20.claim: The singularity is where AI surpasses human intelligence and self-improves

F21.quote: "British mathematician I. J. Good first hypothesized the singularity in a 1965 paper."

F22.quote: "AGI will quickly lead to artificial superintelligence (ASI) in a process known as the intelligence explosion."
F22.claim: AGI will quickly lead to ASI: the intelligence explosion

F23.quote: "There is an emerging consensus among experts that AGI should arrive at least by the end of the decade."
F23.claim: An emerging expert consensus puts AGI by the end of the decade

F24.quote: "American leadership in AI, including open source, is a national security issue."
F24.claim: AI leadership is a national security issue

F25.quote: "The technological singularity is a theoretical scenario where technological growth becomes uncontrollable and irreversible, culminating in profound and unpredictable changes to human civilization."
F25.claim: A theoretical scenario of uncontrollable, irreversible growth

F26.quote: "Ray Kurzweil, one of the most vocal proponents of the singularity, has famously predicted that the singularity is near and will happen by 2045."

F27.quote: "Many critics argue that significant and perhaps insurmountable obstacles stand in the way."
F27.claim: Critics argue there are perhaps insurmountable obstacles

F28.quote: "Skeptics note a decline in the rate of technological innovation, contradicting the exponential growth expected in singularity scenarios."
F28.claim: Skeptics note a decline in innovation's rate

F29.quote: "There is a concern that super intelligent machines could prioritize their own survival and goals over human needs."
F29.claim: Concern that superintelligent machines put their goals over human needs

F30.quote: "AGI and ASI are about the machine. The singularity is about us—specifically, about the moment we lose the ability to see what's coming"
F30.claim: The singularity is about us: the moment we lose the ability to see what's coming

F31.quote: "The singularity is the point past which we can't really predict anything, because at that point it's essentially ASIs running things"
F31.claim: Past the singularity nothing can be predicted, because ASIs run things

F32.quote: "Vinge's thirty-year window from 1993 has basically closed, and his specific claim remains outstanding"
F32.claim: Vinge's thirty-year window has closed; his claim is outstanding

F33.quote: "The Singularity Is Near: When Humans Transcend Biology is a 2005 non-fiction book about artificial intelligence and the future of humanity by inventor and futurist Ray Kurzweil."
F33.claim: Kurzweil's 2005 book on AI and humanity's future

F34.quote: "I set the date for the Singularity—representing a profound and disruptive transformation in human capability—as 2045"
F34.claim: Kurzweil: 'I set the date for the Singularity ... as 2045'

F35.quote: "the Law of Accelerating Returns, which predicts an exponential increase in technologies like computers, genetics, nanotechnology, robotics and artificial intelligence"
F35.claim: The Law of Accelerating Returns predicts exponential technological increase

F36.quote: "the key point about exponential growth is that it never lasts"

F37.quote: "A sequel book, The Singularity Is Nearer, was released on June 25, 2024"

F38.quote: "a point when machine intelligence surpasses human intelligence and begins advancing at a speed we can no longer control or predict"
F38.claim: A point when machine intelligence surpasses ours and advances beyond control or prediction

F39.quote: "AGI is a level of capability. The singularity is what could happen next."
F39.claim: AGI is a capability level; the singularity is what could follow

F40.quote: "The key test is whether AI can improve itself without human direction."
F40.claim: The test is self-improvement without human direction

F41.quote: "we are now, like, in the singularity"
F41.claim: Altman: 'we are now, like, in the singularity'

F42.quote: "features ideas, writing, and technologies of visionaries examining the confluence of accelerating revolutions that will shape the future"
F42.claim: The site presents visionaries on accelerating revolutions

F43.quote: "Good speculated that superhuman intelligence could trigger an “intelligence explosion”"
F43.claim: Good speculated superhuman intelligence could trigger an intelligence explosion

F44.quote: "theoretical condition that could arrive in the near future when a synthesis of several powerful new technologies will radically change the realities in which we find ourselves"
F44.claim: A theoretical condition: a synthesis of technologies radically changing reality

F45.claim: Vinge: an opaque wall across the future

F46.quote: "the new era is simply too different to fit into the classical frame of good and evil"
F46.claim: Vinge: the new era is too different for the frame of good and evil

F47.quote: "It could be amazing or apocalyptic, but we cannot know the details"
F47.claim: It could be amazing or apocalyptic; details unknowable

F48.quote: "in the future we will have the medical tools to banish disease and disease-related death"
F48.claim: Kurzweil: medical tools will banish disease

F49.quote: "the near-future synthesis of nanotech, biotech, infotech, and cognitive science"
